description.value: Two independent fMRI studies examined neural correlates of attentional deployment while healthy adults viewed unpleasant and neutral images with attention directed toward arousing or non-arousing portions.

description.value: Two independent cohorts of healthy adults participated in two studies; participants passively viewed counterbalanced blocks of unpleasant and neutral images, with or without a visual focus instruction, during fMRI.

name.value: Unpleasant non-arousing focus > unpleasant arousing focus (Study 1)

definition.value: Focusing on an unpleasant non-arousing region, compared to an arousing region produced significantly greater activations in parietal regions including the supramarginal gyrus (BA 40), the cuneus, the precuneus (BA 7), as well as greater activation in frontal regions including the inferior frontal gyrus (BA 47), the middle frontal gyrus (BA 10), the superior frontal gyrus (BA 9), the precentral gyrus (BA 6) and the cingulate gyrus (BA 32).

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to passively view image sets and rate the intensity of their negative affect after each set. For no-focus blocks, they were told to “look freely at the following images”; for focus blocks, they were told to “look only at the part of the image within the blue circle.” In Study 2, participants were also asked to fixate on the center of the blue circle.
